descriptionChirho: The last or final item in an ordered sequence or series, whether temporal or ordinal, including 'the last days' as a period and 'the last' as endpoint.
Referring to a later state, time period, or condition contrasted with an earlier one, as in 'the latter rain' or 'the latter end' of a situation.
Directional sense meaning 'western' or 'toward the rear,' reflecting the Hebrew orientation facing east so that 'behind' corresponds to the west.
Describing something that is subsequent or yet to come in time, translated as 'coming after,' 'following,' or 'to come' when referring to future events or periods.
Used adverbially with prepositions (beth, lamed) to form temporal expressions meaning 'at last,' 'in the end,' 'finally,' or 'afterward.'
Substantival use referring to people who come after, later generations, or those who follow, as in 'the latter ones' or 'those who came afterward.'
Used as a divine epithet for God, designating him as 'the Last' in contrast to 'the First,' asserting his eternal sovereignty (Isaiah 44:6, 48:12).
